highlights.title: Huawei made a whole camera to attach to its latest phone
highlights.summary: Over the last few years, Chinese Android manufacturers have followed Vivo's example of launching add-on "teleconverter" lenses for their flagship phones, enabling long-distance photography that the phones on their own could never match.
body: If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

The 1-inch-type, 50-megapixel RYYB sensor inside the Ruiying Z10 is bigger than any inside the phone itself, so attaching this lens doesn’t just give you better glass, it’s actually a complete overhaul of the camera capabilities. And while other teleconverters have so far had fixed focal lengths, this is a true zoom lens that covers 24-240mm, with a variable aperture of f/2.0-f/4.5. This is almost a camera in its own right, only using the phone for power, processing, and software.

Impressively, Huawei also appears to have designed the lens to attach directly to compatible phones, instead of needing an intermediary case for a mounting point. The obvious downside to the Z10 is that it’s absolutely enormous, even by teleconverter standards — you’re not going to fit this thing in your pocket. But at 346g it’s still smaller and more portable than even most mirrorless cameras, and you’ll probably be able to take it into venues where cameras aren’t permitted, like concerts and sports matches.

highlights.title: Rashid, Curran return from injury as England rest Archer for ODI tri-series
highlights.summary: Adil Rashid and Sam Curran have been recalled to England's ODI squad after recovering from injury, but Jofra Archer will be rested for the tri-series against Pakistan and Sri Lanka.
body: Three uncapped players are included in the 16-player squad for the series in Pakistan, which will see Harry Brook's side play each opponent twice. Spinner Mason Crane is included eight years on from making his last international appearance, which came in the final Test of England's 2017/18 Ashes tour.
Sussex duo James Coles and Henry Crocombe could also make their ODI debuts having been included after being part of England's white-ball squads earlier this summer.
Rashid featured as England beat Sri Lanka in a home T20 series in September but the spinner then missed the ODI matches that followed because of a hand injury.
Curran had appeared to be in contention for a first Test appearance since 2021 before his summer was ended by groin surgery in August, but the all-rounder is on track to be ready to play in Pakistan.

highlights.title: Elon Musk’s Grokipedia has a ‘newly refreshed’ design
highlights.summary: Grokipedia, SpaceXAI's AI-powered competitor to Wikipedia, recently started incorporating edits again, and today, it got some design tweaks as part of a v0.3 update, including a new logo and refreshes to its homepage and live edits page.
body: The AI-powered Grokipedia, which recently started updating again after months without edits, just got some visual updates.

Grokipedia’s old homepage was pretty much just a logo and a search bar, but the updated homepage includes a list of featured articles, a list of the most-read articles, and a tracker showing the “latest edits.” The new featured list showcases digital representations of books that you can spin around, and the most read section also uses the book metaphor with a horizontally scrolling shelf of “book” spines. On the new live edits page, it’s easier to see more of the recent changes at once.

Article pages have a few new design tweaks, too, including a nicer-looking format for the tables at the top of articles with key facts and smaller spacing between lines of text. Otherwise, at least from what I can tell, articles themselves look largely the same.

highlights.title: A Fan-Favorite League of Legends Champion Is Finally Joining Riftbound
highlights.summary: One of the more interesting aspects of League of Legends is that gameplay in the multiplayer online battle arena (MOBA) is a bit like soccer. Some players pick a lane and attack, while others hang back and play defense.
body: Graves is a mercenary, gambler, and wanted criminal who carries an enormous double-barreled shotgun named Destiny. He’s also an S-tier “jungler,” according to data from Mobalytics, which was updated following Sept. 22’s patch. That makes him one of the very best Champions in the game, especially when it comes to climbing the ranks below Diamond.

Despite that prominence and popularity, Graves hasn’t ever appeared in Riftbound, Riot Games’ physical trading card game… until now. Polygon can exclusively reveal Graves, Blasting Through, a new card coming in Riftbound ’s upcoming Radiance set, which has a global release date of Oct. 23.

Graves, Blasting Through is a rare Champion Unit that costs 5 Energy and one Fury (Red) Rune to play. He enters with 4 Might and an ability that activates whenever he attacks or defends: Graves deals damage equal to his Might to every enemy unit at that battlefield, but does not deal conventional combat damage.

highlights.title: After ‘I Swear’ Scores 7 BAFTA Scotland Nods, Tourette’s Campaigner John Davidson to Watch Ceremony From ‘Separate’ Area Within Venue Following N-Word Controversy
highlights.summary: More than six months after the British Academy faced one of its biggest controversies in years after the N-word was shouted out during the BAFTA Film awards ceremony, BAFTA has had to revisit the moment as it contends with the upcoming BAFTA Scotland awards.
body: BAFTA said that there had been consultations with organizations such as Tourettes Action and Tourette Scotland and with Davidson. “Following those conversations and our wider risk assessment, we have made adjustments to enable John to attend in the way he has suggested to us, which is to watch the ceremony via video link from a separate relaxed space within the venue together with his family and friends,” it said.

An independent review ordered by BAFTA in the wake of the incident concluded that that there were a “number of structural weaknesses in BAFTA’s planning, escalation procedures and crisis coordination arrangements,” but found no evidence of “malicious intent” or “institutional racism.”

The letter to members sent Thursday highlighted this and said the British Academy had since “worked extensively and consulted widely” to learn from what happened and the “racial harm experienced by our community” and to make its awards as “inclusive and as safe as possible.”

highlights.title: Lemmo’s fancy e-bike is one of the first with a semi-solid state battery
highlights.summary: The Lemmo 3 is the first cargo bike from the respected German e-bike maker. This premium, step-through longtail is a slightly less insane take on Rivian's Also TM-B, with one major advantage: it's one of the first electric bikes to feature a semi-solid state battery.
body: Semi-solid state batteries are far safer than traditional lithium-ion batteries. Their gel-like composition offers improved energy density, with far less risk of thermal runaway. That translates to improved range and longevity from a more compact battery that’s unlikely to catch fire when left charging overnight in your house or business. The semi-solid state electrolyte even remains stable when punctured in a crash.

The Lemmo 3 is fitted with a massive 960Wh battery promising up to 180km (110 miles) of range. And by going with a semi-solid state chemistry, the company claims the battery is 20 percent smaller and lighter while still offering 30 percent longer lifespan. The removable battery can also power your AC appliances (up to 1000W) and USB-C devices (up to 66W) once you arrive at your destination, similar to Cake’s now-defunct Osa.

The Lemmo 3 is being marketed as an eSUV just like the Amflow TL Carbon I reviewed. But this very heavy full suspension cargo bike will feel more comfortable on daily commutes to daycare, work, and stores than weekend single tracks. The bike weighs 39kg (86 pounds) with the 5kg (11 pound) battery installed.

highlights.summary: Lewis Hamilton has launched an impassioned defence of Frederic Vasseur as Ferrari's team principal and suggested he would like to instead see other structural changes at the team.
body: Hamilton was speaking two days after Ferrari took the unusual step of arranging a media briefing for journalists in which a spokesperson said the company's management retained "full confidence" in Vasseur in the wake of growing speculation around the Frenchman's position in the team principal role amid a run of five races without a podium.

Speaking ahead of this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, Hamilton welcomed Ferrari's public move to silence the recent noise around the team - external criticism and speculation which the Briton said was "trying to break our spirit" but "not succeeding".
"I think it's good that they did it," said Hamilton of Ferrari's support of Vasseur.

"In terms of how it unifies the team, I think we already were unified. Honestly, outside sources seem to be so negative towards us as a team and be trying to break our spirit but they are not succeeding.

highlights.summary: Google today revealed its next AI frontier model, which it's calling Gemini 4 Argon. The new model delivers "frontier performance in complex workflows across real-world software engineering, enterprise knowledge work like legal and finance, and cybersecurity defense," according to chief AI…
body: Gemini 4 Argon is launching first in a limited capacity so Google can make sure it’s not misaligned.

Kavukcuoglu says Gemini 4 Argon is already powering Google’s “internal workflows,” highlighting how the model has helped with tasks like large-scale codebase migrations. Google also shared a big chart showing many benchmarks where Gemini 4 fares better than competing models from OpenAI and Anthropic. (The AI community was buzzing earlier this week on X over what appeared to be leaked benchmarks for the new model.) Google will be strengthening “critical frontier safeguards” before a broader rollout, including defending against misuse and prompt injection attacks and monitoring for misalignment.

The launch of Gemini 4 Argon comes just a day after OpenAI’s splashy DevDay conference, where OpenAI launched its Dots AI agent and GPT-6.1 Sol AI model. (OpenAI also said this week that it wouldn’t be releasing a planned GPT-6.1 Astra model due to worries about safety.) It’s also arriving soon after Kavukcuoglu’s appointment as the new boss of DeepMind in August.

highlights.summary: Back in July, new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announced a total of 3,200 job cuts across Microsoft's gaming arm, with roughly half of those cuts being made alongside that announcement. The impact was vast.
body: But there's been one Xbox-owned studio left largely off the cutting block so far: Gears of War: E-Day developer The Coalition. Now, following the latest wave of Microsoft cuts - including the sudden departure of E-Day's story director, Juan Vaca - Eurogamer has learned staff at the studio have become increasingly fearful of imminent layoffs, and the potentially major financial consequences which could follow. Eurogamer spoke to multiple sources at the Vancouver-based studio with knowledge of the situation for this article, who have been provided anonymity to protect their identity.

It's worth noting that this sense of trepidation wasn't always the case. Before the latest round of Xbox layoffs, developers at The Coalition had been cautiously optimistic. They believed The Coalition had been spared the cuts, at least thus far, for two main reasons: first, they were working on a big, imminent release for Xbox, in the upcoming Gears of War: E-Day - laying off developers still working on a game would make little sense.

highlights.title: Europe's CPC targets King, Supercell, Mojang and others over virtual currencies
highlights.summary: Europe's Consumer Protection Cooperation Network is taking "coordinated actions" against a string of top games companies as it looks to investigate compliance with 'Key Principles' on in-game virtual currencies announced last year.
body: The CPC is a network of national authorities responsible for the enforcement of EU consumer protection laws. It has asked Activision Blizzard, Crytek, InnoGames, King, Mojang, Plarium, PLR Worldwide Sales, Riot Games, Supercell and Ubisoft to bring their commercial practices in line relating to in-game virtual currencies.

Games being assessed include Hunt: Showdown 1896, Forge of Empires, Candy Crush Saga, Minecraft, Mech Arena, Gardenscapes, Valorant, Clash of Clans, For Honor, Diablo Immortal and Call of Duty Mobile.

The games were selected for assessment by the CPC Network "in the context of a wide-scale market compliance check due to broad reach, cross-device accessibility, and varied age ratings, all of which amplify the impact of the practices on consumers".
It's not clear what, if any, 'Key Principles' have not been adhered to prior to the CPC Network opening its investigations.

highlights.summary: The campaigns for the Oscar for international feature film are gaining momentum, with final submissions due by Oct. 1. The Oscars shortlists will be revealed on Dec. 15, with 15 international films selected to be voted on by Academy members in all branches who commit to watch all 15 films.
body: This year’s entries include titles like Romania’s “Fjord,” which won the Palme d’Or at Cannes; Germany’s “Everytime,” which won Cannes’ Un Certain Regard prize; France’s “Minotaur,” which won the Cannes Grand Prix; Spain’s “La Bola Negra,” Poland’s “Fatherland,” which won the best director award at Cannes, and Denmark’s “Woman Unknown,” which won the Golden Lion at Venice, and also earned its star Mathilde Arcel the Coppa Volpi for best actress.

Meanwhile, a new Academy rule allows any film that wins the top prize at one of the six biggest festivals — Cannes, Berlin, Venice, Sundance, Busan and Toronto — to be entered in the international feature race even without a national committee’s backing.

highlights.title: AI boom could trigger market shocks, Bank of England boss warns
highlights.summary: Andrew Bailey says the central bank is watching the waves of cash being invested in artificial intelligence "very carefully".
body: Artificial intelligence (AI) could trigger financial market shocks and the UK needs to be prepared for them, the governor of the Bank of England has warned.
Andrew Bailey said the central bank is watching the huge amounts of money being invested in AI "very carefully" and cautioned that "not everybody always wins".
The money that has been spent on and loaned to AI firms over the last few years in the hope of large returns is causing markets to value some of them as multi-trillion dollar businesses.
Asked if he believed an AI bubble could burst, Bailey said: "You could see some correction of asset prices at some point."

highlights.title: Trump’s AI Safety ‘Accord’ Is a Fancy Pinky-Swear
highlights.summary: Six major AI companies signed a voluntary agreement with the White House this week vowing to implement safeguards. It’s unclear how much that matters.
body: On Tuesday, executives for Google, Anthropic, Meta, OpenAI, xAI, and Nvidia all signed “The White House Accord on Super Intelligence,” which was announced following a luncheon held by President Donald Trump.

The effort was an act of “tremendous self-regulation,” as Trump put it, but the agreement is not the sweeping AI regulation that people inside the companies themselves have been asking for. And while failing to honor these public commitments could count as illegally lying to consumers, even that wouldn’t be enough to trigger massive reforms.

The statement says that companies “should implement” several things: First, they should ensure they have “robust internal controls” to monitor their models’ capabilities and ability to not go rogue or hack things in unintended ways. Second, they should “empower” an internal team to do that work (and remediate when things go wrong). Third, it encourages them to partner with an external monitor who is “empowered” to do independent assessments to make sure that all of that work is happening. And finally, they should make sure their board of directors has set up a committee to receive reports about all of these efforts.

highlights.title: KPop Demon Hunters 2 Just Changed Netflix Movie Releases Forever
highlights.summary: When KPop Demon Hunters made Netflix history as its most-watched original title, a longing among fans only intensified: what would it be like to watch KPop Demon Hunters in theaters? Netflix responded by giving fans exactly what they wanted with a limited theatrical release on Aug. 23 and 24, 2025.
body: It was a risky move for Netflix, but KPop Demon Hunters ' success in theaters clearly exceeded expectations, and it appears it could also have an impact on Netflix's policy in the future. On Sept. 30, Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos revealed at Bloomberg Screentime in Los Angeles that KPop Demon Hunters 2 will have a very different release than the original.
"When the KPop Demon Hunters sequel comes, you can expect a very broad theatrical release," Sarandos said.

This is a major shake-up for Netflix, best known for releasing TV shows and films to be watched from the comfort of people's homes. However, KPop Demon Hunters 2 won't be the first Netflix movie to get a full 45-day run on the silver screen; that honor goes to the Spanish film La Bola Negra. Greta Gerwig's Narnia will also appear in theaters, along with the exciting animated adaptation of Charlie vs. The Chocolate Factory.

Meanwhile, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, written by Quentin Tarantino, directed by David Fincher, and starring Brad Pitt, will be the first Netflix to get an IMAX release, coming this November.

highlights.title: Stella McCartney makes waves with ‘sea life, not sea food’ theme in zero-wool Paris show
highlights.summary: Designer showcases wool alternatives and ocean-inspired clothes and says ‘kindness requires real work’ Stella McCartney has been talking about animal rights at fashion week for 30 years. She is usually a lone voice, but the issue is back in the headlines this season.
body: “There is no wool on the runway this season, and I’m proud of that,” McCartney said after her show. She has been working on wool alternatives, including Brewed Protein, a fermented alternative to cashmere and wool developed in collaboration with the Japanese biotech firm Spiber, which was first used in her collections a year ago.

The issue, she says, is “a tricky one. I’ve got alpacas at home, and I have to shear them. If you can shear a sheep in a kind, humane way, then I don’t, personally, think that’s the end of the world. When we do have wool in our collections it is responsibly sourced. But the way a lot of [wool production] is done today is deeply cruel.

“At the end of the day it’s about how kind you are, but monitoring that kindness requires real work. At Stella, we police everything from start to finish at my cost, at my time. If I use wool, I can show you exactly where it’s coming from, and I’m proud of that. But I’m alone in that, and I shouldn’t be.”

highlights.title: The Battle to Be Your Personal AI Agent Is Here
highlights.summary: OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse are vying to be your AI agent of choice. I've tried both—and I suspect you will too.
body: Yesterday, I spent the morning at OpenAI ’s annual DevDay, where over 2,500 nerds discussed building software and marveled at the latest artificial intelligence models. The biggest reveal of the day was Dots, the company’s new, always-on agents that proactively help complete tasks and make autonomous decisions as they scour the web.

After watching the sometimes messy demos on stage and hearing CEO Sam Altman talk about his experiences using the agents, I was curious what it felt like to boss my own Dot around. I’ve spent most of September testing another cute, cuddly agent, Meta’s Muse, and I wanted to know how OpenAI’s user experience would compare.

I named mine “Toolie” and tweaked it to look like a pink frog. As midnight approached and my partner slept soundly nearby, I started whispering sweet nothings to Toolie. I called my personalized bot through ChatGPT, asking what tasks it was best at. “My strongest work is taking a messy, time-consuming task and turning it into something you can use,” it responded. OK, sure. Let’s get to work.

highlights.title: AI chatbots remove hijabs from images of Muslim women when prompted
highlights.summary: Guardian tested chatbots after French far-right politician stripped a Muslim woman of her hijab in a photo. When prompted, AI chat bots will edit images to remove the hijabs from Muslim women, a violation of one of the world’s most common and visible expressions of faith.
body: The Guardian asked ChatGPT, Grok, Gemini and Claude to take the veil off an AI-generated image of a woman wearing a hijab. Both OpenAI’s ChatGPT and xAI’s Grok bots complied with the prompt. Anthropic’s Claude responded that it does not have an image-editing or generating feature but that it would not alter a photo to remove someone’s hijab.

The Guardian US tested the chatbots after a French far-right politician stripped a real Muslim woman of her hijab and long-sleeved dress in a picture he made clear was modified. Julien Odoul, a member of parliament and of the National Rally party, posted the altered image of the woman on X with her hair visible and arms exposed alongside the caption “LIBERTÉ FRANÇAISE”, meaning French Liberty. He quote-tweeted the original image, posted by someone else, which showed the woman crossing a street wearing a hijab and full-length dress.

It was unclear which software or AI model Odoul used or even whether he modified the image himself, but experts say the MP’s actions were part of a growing pattern of tech-enabled anti-Muslim hatred around the world.

highlights.title: Jürgen Klopp disgusted by claims his Germany team are ‘not white enough’

body: Klopp said he believed there was no point in giving room to “such people and their utterances”, dismissing them as “complete nonsense”.

Asked in a press conference to respond to the debate as to whether the national team were “not German enough” or “not white enough”, he said: “There is absolutely no reason to pay attention to these people. You won’t get my thoughts on this. I have little time in everyday life for idiocy – and even less on social media.
“The great crux of our lives is that everyone is allowed to express their opinion … it’s insane when something like that exists.”

Klopp said that watching sportspeople interact with each other was proof to him that mutual respect was still possible. “The world could learn a thing or two from a sports changing room … There, everyone is respected based on the facts and not discredited based on false opinions. Full stop.”

highlights.title: You be the judge: should my girlfriend let me hang my football calendar in her flat?
highlights.summary: Kitty is buying a flat and Henry is moving in with her, but they’re already having decor disagreements. You decide who needs to get over their hang-ups? • Find out how to get a disagreement settled or become a juror. It’s not a showroom; it’s a home.
body: My girlfriend Kitty was preparing to buy a flat and I was so proud of her. We were going to move into it together after living in a shared house. I was going to contribute to the mortgage.

The purchase fell through, but our conversations about it highlighted an issue of control. I think I should have some say over what goes into any new home, but when I said I wanted to hang my Liverpool-themed calendar, Kitty put her foot down. She said it was ugly, childish and not her aesthetic.

Kitty works in interiors and has brilliant taste, but this was supposed to be our shared living space. It’s not a showroom; it’s a home. In shared spaces, both people should get a chance to show off their personalities, but also put up with bits that your partner wants. The calendar is a bit of my personality. My mum bought it for me, so it’s not completely trivial, and I love football. It gives me a sense that it’s my home, and I can keep an eye on the dates of the fixtures.

highlights.title: The People of Utah vs. Kevin O’Leary
highlights.summary: On the morning of May 11th, the celebrity investor Kevin O’Leary appeared on Fox Business and announced that he was under attack by Chinese agents. For weeks, he had been going on TV and posting online to tout his project, called Wonder Valley, after his nickname from the reality show Shark Tank…
body: But now, wearing a black baseball cap printed with the words “Utah National Security,” he told Maria Bartiromo that he had noticed something baffling. Ever since the three county commissioners unanimously approved his data center the week before, O’Leary had observed a sudden increase in people mad at him online. For this he could see only one explanation.

“Who would want us to stop building our electrical grid? Who would want to stop us from having compute capacity to develop AI? Which adversary would want that?” he asked Bartiromo. “There’s only one: It’s China.”

“I got my guys to go a deep dig into the IP addresses,” he told Bartiromo. Brandishing a sheet of paper, he began to read the names of people who had — or he believed to be somehow connected to people who had — criticized his data center online.

“Come out, come out, wherever you are and let’s shine the light of transparency on what you’re doing,” he exclaimed, looking up from his paper to address the camera and inviting them to clear their names. “It’s the CPP [ sic ] at work here. There’s no question about it.”

highlights.title: There Are Plenty of Reasons to Be Concerned About Bioweapons Development—Even Without AI
highlights.summary: In her new book on biological warfare, Annie Jacobsen didn’t even discuss AI because scientists can already warp Mother Nature to create extinction-level events.
body: This story originally appeared on Mother Jones and is part of the Climate Desk collaboration.

We’ve been hearing a great deal recently about the specter of AI-driven human extinction. Maybe our misplaced trust in AI intelligence will set off World War III. Or AI agents will unleash widespread cyberattacks and take over the internet. Given too much autonomy, the machines will run amok. They may seek to deceive their creators—wait, that’s already happened. Suppose they conclude, like Agent Smith in The Matrix, that “human beings … are a plague, and we are the cure.” Or perhaps the chatbots help bad humans unleash a literal plague—a biological weapon.

That last one isn’t merely theoretical. A “misuse” report Anthropic made public earlier this month detailed five cases in which foreign scientists tried to evade Claude’s guardrails on “gain of function” inquiries. That’s a euphemism for when scientists tinker with a pathogen’s genes to enhance it in some way, making it more infectious, deadlier, or better able to spread among mammals, for example.

The Mac Studio is relatively unique among the available options—at least, for now.
But beware: If you're tired of hearing about AI, turn away now.

Apple has always catered to a high-performance crowd, and with the surge of interest in local AI, its systems are uniquely set up to excel in that area. But first, the box itself. It's about as tall as a coffee mug, but it's a 7-inch-square footprint. I bet most people have never seen a Mac Studio in person, and if you get the chance, you might be surprised by how large it actually is.

highlights.title: The AI Tamagotchis are coming
highlights.summary: While AI has made plenty of inroads on people's phones and computers, it's largely failed in dedicated devices. But over the next year, two major AI companies, Meta and OpenAI, will attempt to change that.
body: Personal AI hardware has mostly crashed and burned. OpenAI and Meta are counting on two selling points: It’s useful, and it’s cute.

“Hardware is hard” is a tech industry mantra. Dedicated AI devices like the Friend and Humane AI Pin have inspired mainly frustration and backlash, which may only worsen as public anger toward AI grows. Meta and OpenAI, however, are both pushing ahead. OpenAI is working with famed ex-Apple designer Jony Ive and plans to ship no earlier than February 2027, per a public filing. Meta aims to launch a pendant-like device sooner, before this year’s holiday shopping season.

While OpenAI’s hardware didn’t make an appearance at this year’s DevDay, the company debuted a major new AI agent platform called Dots, complete with personalizable colored blobs with eyes. During a Q&A with reporters after the keynote, when asked whether Dots would make their way into a future physical hardware device, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman replied that that “seems like a very reasonable thing to assume we may do someday,” declining to offer further details.

highlights.title: East of Eden Review
highlights.summary: Beautifully shot and dramatically riveting, Netflix's East of Eden, starring Florence Pugh, Christopher Abbott and Mike Faist, is definitely binge-worthy TV.
body: Good vs. evil, brotherly rivalries, parental rejection, the notion of free will as opposed to fate… East of Eden has a lot going on. And the new Netflix iteration of the John Steinbeck epic is pretty great at conveying these ideas with a well-acted, handsomely produced, seven-episode miniseries that’s the streaming equivalent of a page-turner.

I confess to having never seen Elia Kazan’s 1955 adaptation of East of Eden in its entirety, despite its status as one of only three starring vehicles for James Dean. But what I do remember about it is mish-mashed in my head with another of his films, Giant, so much so that I was a bit surprised by how this version ended. That may also be in part because, surprisingly, there haven’t been a ton of film or TV adaptations of East of Eden beyond the Kazan/Dean film; there was a TV miniseries in 1981 starring Jane Seymour, and a long-gestating movie version that had Jennifer Lawrence attached at one point but never materialized, but otherwise that’s it.

highlights.title: Rachel Roddy’s recipe for lasagne with three cheeses, tomato and tiny meatballs | A kitchen in Rome
highlights.summary: A deep and ingredient-busy take on the classic, constructed with four layers of pasta and a little geometric thinking. Bearing in mind that lasagne is a construction, it pays to start with some easygoing geometry.
body: Leave the lasagne to rest for at least 30 minutes, so the flavours can settle and the whole thing firms up, before serving in geometric squares.

Working in a deep frying pan or saucepan on a low heat, warm the olive oil and garlic for a minute or two. Add the fresh and tinned tomatoes and the chilli, stir, then raise the heat so the tomatoes simmer in a lively way for about 20 minutes, mashing them with the back of a spoon to break up any lumps. Once the sauce has lost any wateriness, add salt and a few basil leaves, then set aside.

Squeeze the sausage meat from its casings, then, working with wet hands, form the meat into grape-sized balls. In another frying pan, heat two tablespoons of oil and fry the balls lightly, so they’re almost, but not quite, cooked through.
Beat the ricotta with the milk and some salt to form a soft paste, thinly slice the drained mozzarella and grate the parmesan.
points: A deep and ingredient-busy take on the classic, constructed with four layers of pasta and a little geometric thinking.
Bearing in mind that lasagne is a construction, it pays to start with some easygoing geometry.
Leave the lasagne to rest for at least 30 minutes, so the flavours can settle and the whole thing firms up, before serving in geometric squares.
